chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The greatest wealth is contentment (or disengagement) from what is in the hands of people.

key_terms.الْيَأْسُ: Despair, disengagement, or ceasing to hope/desire

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of true wealth in Shia Islam according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) redefines wealth through the lens of psychological detachment, asserting that true richness lies in ceasing to covet what is in the hands of others. This concept aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'ghina al-nafs' (self-sufficiency), distinguishing it from mere material abundance by highlighting the eradication of dependency on external possessions. It serves as a practical guide for cultivating inner peace and spiritual independence, core tenets of asceticism (zuhd) in Islamic ethics.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 342. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The biggest wealth is that one should not have an eye on what others possess.
